claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: In `src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py`, SQL example pairs that a memory backend over-returns are dropped without any signal. The `omitted` flag is set from the text-memory count alone at line 225, while pairs are already cut to five at line 167, so `_format_context` never sees that a pair was lost. If a backend returns more than five usable pairs and the text memories stay within their own limit, examples disappear and neither the prompt notice nor a log line records it. No omission of any kind is written to the logger, so an operator cannot tell a server whose caps keep evicting examples from one that simply found no match. The new test at `tests/unit/test_memory_context_boundary.py:78` over-returns both texts and pairs in one call, so its `assert "omitted" in out` is satisfied by the text branch alone and would still pass if the pair branch reported nothing. (raised by 3/5 agents)

So omitted is not set whenever any candidate is dropped: if only pairs exceed the limit (texts within limit, budget fits), no omission marker (_CONTEXT_OMITTED, line 37, 'Some retrieved memory was omitted...') is emitted.
